abstracts.abstract: This paper presents a fundamental reconceptualization of compositional verification through a game-theoretic framework that fundamentally transforms how system components are analyzed. Traditional assume-guarantee reasoning relies on fixed contracts between components, but this approach treats component interactions as strategic games where each module optimizes its behavior against environmental assumptions. We introduce the concept of compositional attractor synthesis, where system-level properties are verified by computing winning strategies in product games formed from component specifications. The theoretical foundation establishes that for regular properties in ω-regular languages, the compositional game solution coincides with traditional verification when contracts satisfy consistency and completeness conditions. Our framework enables verification of open systems by reducing it to solving infinite-duration games on finite game graphs. The approach demonstrates particular strength in handling real-time and hybrid systems where continuous dynamics interact with discrete control decisions. We prove that the synthesis procedure terminates with minimal fixpoint computations and provide complexity analysis showing exponential improvement over brute-force product exploration for certain system topologies. This paradigm shift from verification-as-checking to verification-as-synthesis represents a fundamental departure from conventional model checking methodologies.

Interpolation-based model checking has proven effective for software verification but suffers from spurious counterexamples when using conventional proof-generation techniques. This paper introduces a novel interpolation scheme based on recursive proof tree analysis that significantly improves the precision of BMC+ interpolation for programs with complex control flow. Our approach decomposes the transition relation into hierarchically structured interpolants that preserve path-sensitive information across loop unrollings. We establish theoretical foundations showing that the proposed interpolation hierarchy yields over-approximations that are strictly more precise than those from standard MCI procedures for a substantial class of programs. The key innovation lies in a new interpolation operator that respects the syntactic structure of transition formulas while maintaining logical soundness. We prove that the resulting abstract interpretation framework dominates existing interpolation schemes in precision while maintaining comparable computational complexity. Experimental evaluation on benchmark suites from the SV-COMP competition demonstrates average improvements of 34% in verification time and 28% reduction in memory consumption compared to state-of-the-art interpolation-based model checkers. The technique scales particularly well for embedded systems software with interrupt handlers and device driver code, where traditional approaches frequently timeout or produce false alarms.

We present Veriflow, a novel verification platform that fundamentally redefines the integration of heterogeneous formal methods through a unified symbolic execution engine. Unlike existing tools that treat model checking, theorem proving, and property checking as separate concerns requiring manual coordination, Veriflow provides a common intermediate representation that enables seamless migration between verification techniques during a single verification session. The architecture introduces adaptive verification strategy selection, where the system automatically switches between bounded model checking, k-induction, and interactive theorem proving based on real-time analysis of proof progress. The platform targets cyber-physical systems with particular emphasis on hybrid dynamics where continuous physical processes interact with discrete controllers. Veriflow incorporates a constraint solving backend that combines SAT/SMT solving with interval arithmetic for handling real-valued variables in hybrid system models. We demonstrate the system's capabilities through case studies in automotive control software and medical device certification, showing that the adaptive strategy outperforms monolithic verification approaches in both verification time and proof completion rates. The tool supports industry-standard modeling languages including Simulink subsets and provides integration with existing development workflows through plugin architectures.

This paper presents an extended implementation of an SMT-based model checker with specialized support for real-time and embedded system verification, substantially enhancing the state-of-the-art in automated formal analysis. Our system augments the core model checking engine with purpose-built decision procedures for timing analysis, including worst-case execution time bounds, clock synchronization drift, and priority inheritance protocols. The architecture introduces incremental verification with counterexample-guided abstraction refinement specifically tailored for programs with timing-sensitive control flow. We detail the engineering decisions enabling the tool to handle industrial-scale embedded software with millions of lines of code while maintaining the precision required for safety-critical certification. The implementation extends CBMC with theories for timed automata and introduces a lazy encoding scheme that postpones timing constraints until abstraction refinement determines their necessity. Experimental results on automotive benchmark suites show a 45% reduction in verification time compared to external timing analysis tools used in combination with conventional model checkers. The system has been successfully applied to verify automotive brake-by-wire controllers and flight control software, producing machine-checkable proof certificates suitable for DO-178C certification evidence. We provide detailed performance analysis and guidelines for integrating the tool into existing development processes.
